findings.passage: He expects to be "disappointed," hears his "cynical nature" first, and says his brain "goes cynical and dark" at his own birthday party.
findings.problem: The main Six-over-Seven discriminator rests on the thesis-friendly half of a 2019 answer. On Back to One (S29), after "I've grinded enough to like be disappointed enough times that I never, I will never put my eggs in any basket" and the hype explanation, he corrects himself at about 0:58:30: "So, in a healthy way, I think I've been disappointed enough, you know? And I don't even, I shouldn't even say disappointed 'cause that's not even the really, that's by no means is a feeling that I felt in that." (Research medium.en vtt at 0:58:36; reproduced independently with whisper.cpp small.en on a fresh clip.) The article omits the correction and paraphrases the line as "He expects to be 'disappointed'". Reframing a letdown so it was not felt as one is close to the Seven move the next paragraph says he does not make ("A Seven ... reframes a letdown before it lands. Abbott leans the other way"). The same clipped line feeds "braces for disappointment" in the type answer and type FAQ, "braces for letdowns" in the Type 8 FAQ, C136, and the persona title. This sentence is also missing from the claim inventory, so coverage is incomplete.
findings.acceptance_test: Near the eggs block quote, the Bracing section reports his self-correction (quote "I shouldn't even say disappointed" or paraphrase it faithfully, attributed to Back to One 2019). "He expects to be 'disappointed'" is removed or reworded so it no longer claims an expectation of disappointment he disowned. The Six-over-Seven paragraph explicitly weighs the correction (for example, that the 2019 forecast leans as much toward reframing as toward bracing, leaving the 2026 joke lines and the "cynical and dark" party line as the forecast evidence) and keeps the confidence and Seven-live language honest. The type answer, type FAQ, Type 8 FAQ and persona_title do not state more than the reweighed evidence supports. The sentence is added to the evidence inventory as an interpretation claim, and C16, C33, C45, C116, C136 and C144 inferences are updated.

findings.passage: Nor do they usually build a second trade on the side the way he did during _Girls_, asking, "do I want to only rely on it?"
findings.problem: The fallback-trade discriminator omits his stated reasons, which point away from security. On Happy Sad Confused (S18, about 0:29:40-0:30:20; confirmed by an independent large-v3-turbo pass) the host asks "why did you have to, for money?" and he answers "No, I didn't ... it wasn't that much money at that time." He explains: "I was trying to get in touch with like whatever working roots or manhood," calls it "an early identity crisis", and says being noticed for the show "made me sort of act out in certain ways." The article keeps only "do I want to only rely on it?" and labels the jobs a fallback trade ("keeps a fallback" in the type answer and type FAQ; "kept a fallback trade during Girls" in the Type 8 FAQ, one of only three reasons given there for Six over Eight). Seeking "working roots or manhood" echoes his "I'm a man. I don't do this kind of shit" and fits the Eight reading at least as well. This is a boundary error between reported fact and inferred motive.
findings.acceptance_test: The Italian-ice/carpentry passage reports that he said he did not need the jobs for money and that he was "trying to get in touch with ... working roots or manhood" (faithful paraphrase acceptable). The Six-over-Eight paragraph either reweighs "do I want to only rely on it?" against those stated reasons or stops counting the side jobs as Six evidence. "Keeps a fallback" (type answer, type FAQ) and "kept a fallback trade during Girls" (Type 8 FAQ) are reworded or removed to match. C66, C67, C116, C142 and the type_hypothesis discriminator text are updated.

findings.passage: That pattern is partial. _Girls_ is the only multi-year offer in the record, and he carried _Catch-22_ and _Salesman_, which neither he nor his friends built.
findings.problem: "Carried ... Salesman" overstates a featured role: his Tony nomination was for Best Featured Actor and Nathan Lane played Willy (S23). The preceding list, "He finishes what he signs up for: ... a Broadway run of Salesman", is not backed by any opened source showing he played through the end of the 22-week engagement that began March 6, 2026 (his daughter was born in July 2026).
findings.acceptance_test: Salesman is described as a role he played (for example, "played Biff in Salesman") rather than one he carried. Either an opened source confirms he finished the Salesman run, or it is dropped from the "finishes what he signs up for" list. C131 and C132 are updated.

findings.passage: That 2019 conversation, recorded live in Brooklyn weeks after _Catch-22_ premiered, holds most of the anxiety talk in his record.
findings.problem: The Filmmaker page (S29) dates publication to June 4, 2019 and calls it a live event in Brooklyn, but gives no recording date. "Weeks after Catch-22 premiered" (May 17, 2019) is an inference; the host's "I don't know if you guys have seen it" suggests the show was out, but no source dates the recording.
findings.acceptance_test: The sentence uses a date the source states (for example, "a live Brooklyn taping released in June 2019, weeks after Catch-22 premiered") or marks the timing as approximate. C84 is updated to match.
